title: Semester and Detention
premise: Zephyrine Sandoval, a scholarship student at Hollowmere Academy, has spent four years keeping his head down and counting days to graduation. When a teacher pairs him with his nemesis, wealthy legacy student Odile Vane, for a semester project on the town's founding tradition — the Lantern Vigil — they uncover evidence that the tradition is built on a covered-up death and that the academy will destroy the records before graduation. As Zephyrine digs deeper to save what's true of the tradition without erasing what it means to the town, he discovers his own scholarship was funded by the family responsible, making him both beneficiary and threat. In the end, Zephyrine and Odile expose the truth at the final Vigil, sacrificing his scholarship and her inheritance, but forging a found family among the town's forgotten descendants who rebuild the tradition honestly.
about_author: Wren Eriksen is a former boarding school scholarship kid who writes about institutions, inheritance, and the kids who slip through both. They live in a coastal town that holds one lantern festival a year and guard its history jealously.

chapters.title: Forty-Seven Days of Nothing
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Opening day of senior spring at Hollowmere Academy; Zephyrine maps his survival routine — invisible, punctual, unremarkable — while counting down to graduation. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking a fierce hunger to simply leave intact.

chapters.title: The Vane Girl Smiles Like a Lock
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Odile Vane, fourth-generation legacy and his longtime tormentor-by-indifference, publicly dismantles his scholarship essay in seminar. Establish their enmity. Beat: humiliation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Ms. Okonkwo announces the semester capstone: document the Lantern Vigil, the town's founding tradition, in pairs. She reads 'Sandoval and Vane' aloud. Both protest; she refuses. Beat: trapped fury and a spark of reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile proposes strict division of labor: she takes archives, he takes interviews. She needs an A to secure her family's board seat; he needs the credit to graduate. Beat: cold professionalism hiding mutual wariness.

chapters.title: What the Vigil Is Supposed to Be
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. First fieldwork: the town's Vigil night retelling, where hundreds float lanterns for Elias Marsh, the founder's lost son. Zephyrine watches the town believe something beautiful together. Beat: unexpected tenderness toward a story he never owned.

chapters.title: The Archive Basement
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile pulls founding records and finds a gap: the year of the first Vigil has pages razored out of the ledger. Her grandfather's name appears on the removal authorization. Beat: unease she can't file away.

chapters.title: Interview with Mrs. Adeyemi
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A retired town schoolteacher hints that the first Vigil wasn't for a lost son but for someone the town failed. She stops mid-sentence when her grandson walks in. Beat: the thrill and guilt of prying.

chapters.title: Truce Over Bad Coffee
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Comparing notes at a diner, Zephyrine and Odile realize their halves form one picture: a deliberate erasure. They agree to a real truce. Beat: grudging respect, first crack in the enmity.

chapters.title: The Scholarship Letter
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Digging into funding records, Zephyrine finds his scholarship endowed by the Vane family trust — earmarked, oddly, the same year the ledger was cut. Beat: dread; the ground tilts under his meritocracy.

chapters.title: Why I Hate This School
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flashback chapter: Odile's childhood under her grandfather's expectations, and the older Vane cousin who left in disgrace after asking questions about the Vigil. Beat: sympathy reframe; her cruelty revealed as armor.

chapters.title: The Cousin Who Left
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Tracking the disgraced cousin, Theo Vane, now living two towns over, Zephyrine gets three minutes on a porch: 'Ask who the first lantern was really for.' Beat: ominous invitation.

chapters.title: Elias Marsh Had a Daughter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Parish records reveal Elias Marsh had two children — the son celebrated by the Vigil, and a daughter, Ruth, written out entirely. Beat: revelation; the tradition honors the wrong child.

chapters.title: Ruth's Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the church basement, Odile finds Ruth Marsh's own account book: she kept the Vigil alive for decades, unpaid and unnamed, until the Vanes' academy absorbed it. Beat: grief for an erased woman; personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: Midterm Sabotage
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Their draft presentation vanishes from the shared drive; Ms. Okonkwo warns them someone on the board has asked about their project. Beat: paranoia; the institution notices them.

chapters.title: Headmaster Crane Invites Them to Tea
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The headmaster charmingly suggests they narrow the project to 'the Vigil's positive civic impact.' He mentions Zephyrine's funding by name. Beat: velvet threat; the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Found Family, Temporary Terms
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine's diner friends — Marisol, Dev, and Mrs. Adeyemi's grandson Kofi — become an unofficial research crew. First time Zephyrine has ever had people. Beat: warmth; the loneliness cracks open.

chapters.title: What Happened in 1893
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Assembled testimony: Ruth Marsh drowned during a flood while saving Vigil stores; the town, led by the first Vanes, blamed her brother's negligence and canonized him instead. Beat: horror at how cleanly a lie becomes heritage.

chapters.title: Odile Confronts Her Grandfather
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile demands answers at Vane House; her grandfather admits the cover-up as 'stewardship' — the lie keeps the town alive, the academy funded, order intact. Beat: betrayal; loyalty vs. truth crystallizes inside her own bloodline.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Headmaster Crane offers Zephyrine a full ride to any college he names — if the project stays cosmetic. Zephyrine, who has nothing, is offered everything. Beat: temptation rendered in unbearable detail.

chapters.title: Zephyrine Says Yes
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Terrified of losing graduation, Zephyrine accepts and tells no one. He drafts the sanitized version. Beat: self-betrayal; the reader's stomach drops with his.

chapters.title: Kofi Finds Out
chapters.summary: Kofi's POV (first non-lead POV). Kofi discovers the sanitized draft and confronts Zephyrine: 'You get to leave. Ruth Marsh never did.' Beat: righteous anger; found family fractures.

chapters.title: Odile Chooses Sides
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile learns of Zephyrine's deal and, instead of exposing him, burns her own bridge — she tells the board she'll present the true history alone, forfeiting her endorsement. Beat: her arc's hinge; loyalty chosen over inheritance.

chapters.title: The Razed Pages
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo Vane mails them what he stole years ago: photographs of the missing ledger pages, including the removal order signed by three families — Vane, Crane, and the academy's first benefactor. Beat: proof in hand, and a countdown begins.

chapters.title: They're Coming for the Records
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The pair learn the archive basement is scheduled for 'remediation' before graduation — physical destruction of everything. Zephyrine's guilt curdles into action. Beat: fear converted to purpose.

chapters.title: Breaking Into Our Own School
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Nighttime infiltration with Marisol, Dev, and Kofi to photograph every record. Near-catastrophe when a night guard nearly catches Dev. Beat: heist tension; the crew bonds under adrenaline.

chapters.title: Ms. Okonkwo's Door
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Caught fleeing, Zephyrine confesses everything to Ms. Okonkwo — including his deal with Crane. Instead of reporting him, she reveals she assigned the pairing deliberately: she's Ruth Marsh's great-granddaughter. Beat: stunning reversal; the teacher was the architect.

chapters.title: The Plan for the Final Vigil
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The group plans to tell the truth publicly at the final Vigil, when the whole town attends — renaming it for Ruth, restoring her ledger. Odile will speak as a Vane. Beat: hope with teeth; everyone knows the cost.

chapters.title: Crane Suspends the Project
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The board cancels the capstone presentation outright and threatens expulsion for 'archive tampering.' Zephyrine's acceptance of Crane's offer is voided — he'll lose the scholarship anyway. Beat: despair; the price comes due regardless.

chapters.title: What Zephyrine Owes
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Alone, Zephyrine reckons with why he took the deal: not cowardice but exhaustion — survival has been his whole personality. Kofi sits with him without forgiving him yet. Beat: quiet reckoning; shame met with patience.

chapters.title: Marisol's Lanterns
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The town's lantern-makers quietly agree to make this year's lanterns bear Ruth's name alongside Elias's — the town itself begins choosing truth. Beat: the found family widens into a found town.

chapters.title: Odile's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile's grandfather offers her everything back if she recants publicly. She asks him instead to attend the Vigil and hear Ruth's name read. His silence is not a no. Beat: fragile, human hope inside the antagonist family.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Final preparations; Crane locks the archive and posts security. The crew accepts some of them may be expelled by morning. Zephyrine and Odile share an honest conversation about fear. Beat: calm before the storm; tenderness without romance-forced resolution.

chapters.title: The Final Vigil Begins
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Hundreds gather at the water. The traditional reading of Elias's story proceeds — and then Odile walks to the podium uninvited. Beat: held breath; the point of no return.

chapters.title: Ruth Marsh's Name
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile reads Ruth's ledger aloud, confessing her family's crime by name. Murmurs, anger, and then Mrs. Adeyemi stands, then the lantern-makers, then dozens. Beat: catharsis; truth landing like a bell toll.

chapters.title: Crane's Last Move
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Crane attempts to have the students removed; Ms. Okonkwo presents the photographed records and the board's own signatures to the assembled town and press. Crane's coalition collapses. Beat: climax resolution; institutional power breaking against communal witness.

chapters.title: Aftermath at the Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The town floats lanterns for Ruth. Odile's grandfather arrives late, stands at the edge, and lights one. Zephyrine watches the tradition survive precisely because it changed. Beat: awe; grief and repair in the same breath.

chapters.title: Expulsion Hearings
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The board, newly reconstituted, reduces penalties; Zephyrine still loses the scholarship but gains a Ruth Marsh Memorial Fund established by Theo Vane and townspeople — enough for state college. Beat: bittersweet justice; nothing restored fully, everything changed.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine crosses the stage having stopped counting days somewhere along the way. Odile sits beside him as co-author of the published capstone: 'The Two Children of Elias Marsh.' Beat: earned arrival; the sentence served becomes a beginning.

chapters.title: What We Kept
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Epilogue: summer in the town, the Vigil committee reborn with Ruth's descendants and the friend group at its center. Odile and Zephyrine are no longer nemesis or project partners — just family, chosen. Beat: warm resolution; loyalty and truth reconciled.

chapters.title: Semester's End
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Final short chapter: Zephyrine packs one bag for state college, leaves the countdown calendar blank, and adds a new page titled 'Year One.' Beat: quiet hope; survival transformed into living.
